chunks: From him, from Yusuf ibn al-Harith, from Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Minqari, from Musa ibn Ayyub al-Ghafiqi, from his uncle Iyas ibn Amir al-Ghafiqi, from Uqbah ibn Amir al-Juhani, that he said:

When the verse 'So glorify the name of your Lord, the Great' was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to us: 'Make it in your bowing (ruku'). And when the verse 'Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High' was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to us: 'Make it in your prostration (sujud).'
ai.seo_question: What are the recommended supplications for ruku and sujud in Shia prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the Sunnah of specific glorifications in prayer, linking 'Subhana Rabbiya al-Azim' to Ruku' and 'Subhana Rabbiya al-A'la' to Sujud. While the summary attributes these to Surah Al-Waqi'ah and Al-A'la, Shia scholarship traditionally associates 'Al-A'la' with Surah 87 and 'Al-Azim' with Surah 56, emphasizing the Prophet's direct instruction to align recitation with the revealed verses' themes of divine majesty and transcendence.
